claim: The chloroplast proteome contains thousands of different proteins that are encoded by the nuclear genome.
source: The chloroplast proteome contains thousands of different proteins that are encoded by the nuclear genome.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about chloroplast protein composition.

claim: Nuclear-encoded chloroplast proteins are imported into the chloroplast via the action of the TOC translocase and associated downstream systems.
source: These proteins are imported into the chloroplast via the action of the TOC translocase and associated downstream systems.
evidence: This is established knowledge about chloroplast protein import mechanisms.

claim: The stability of the TOC complex is dynamically regulated by the ubiquitin-dependent chloroplast-associated protein degradation pathway.
source: Our recent work has revealed that the stability of the TOC complex is dynamically regulated by the ubiquitin-dependent chloroplast-associated protein degradation pathway.
evidence: This claim references prior work by the authors and is supported by citation to their previous research.

claim: The TOC complex is regulated by the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) system.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the TOC complex is also regulated by the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) system.
evidence: This is the main finding of the manuscript, supported by multiple experiments presented in the results section.

claim: Arabidopsis mutants representing almost the entire SUMO conjugation pathway can partially suppress the phenotype of ppi1.
source: Arabidopsis mutants representing almost the entire SUMO conjugation pathway can partially suppress the phenotype of ppi1, a pale-yellow mutant lacking the Toc33 protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic experiments shown in Figures 1, 2, and 4.

claim: Suppression of ppi1 by SUMO mutants is linked to increased abundance of TOC proteins.
source: This suppression is linked to increased abundance of TOC proteins and improvements in chloroplast development.
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1I-K.

claim: Suppression of ppi1 by SUMO mutants is linked to improvements in chloroplast development.
source: This suppression is linked to increased abundance of TOC proteins and improvements in chloroplast development.
evidence: This is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1C-F.

claim: The SUMO system directly regulates TOC protein stability.
source: Moreover, data from molecular and biochemical experiments support a model in which the SUMO system directly regulates TOC protein stability.
evidence: This is supported by BiFC and immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Chloroplasts are membrane-bound organelles that house photosynthesis in all green plants.
source: The chloroplast is a membrane-bound organelle that houses photosynthesis in all green plants (Jarvis and Lopez-Juez, 2013).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Chloroplasts are the integrated descendants of a cyanobacterial ancestor that entered the eukaryotic lineage via endosymbiosis.
source: Chloroplasts have an unusual evolutionary history – they are the integrated descendants of a cyanobacterial ancestor that entered the eukaryotic lineage via endosymbiosis.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about chloroplast evolution.

claim: Almost all of the proteins required for chloroplast development and function are encoded by the nuclear genome.
source: Although chloroplasts retain small genomes, almost all of the proteins required for chloroplast development and function are now encoded by the central, nuclear genome (Jarvis, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Nuclear-encoded chloroplast proteins must be imported into the organelle after synthesis in the cytosol.
source: These proteins must be imported into the organelle after synthesis in the cytosol, and this import is mediated by the coordinate action of the TOC and TIC complexes (the translocons at the outer and inner envelope membranes of chloroplasts; Jarvis, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Protein import into chloroplasts is mediated by the coordinate action of the TOC and TIC complexes.
source: These proteins must be imported into the organelle after synthesis in the cytosol, and this import is mediated by the coordinate action of the TOC and TIC complexes (the translocons at the outer and inner envelope membranes of chloroplasts; Jarvis, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The TOC complex contains three major components: Toc75, Toc33, and Toc159.
source: The TOC complex contains three major components: the Omp85 (outer membrane protein, 85 kDa)-related protein, Toc75, which serves as a membrane channel (Schnell et al., 1994; Tranel et al., 1995), and two GTPase-domain receptor proteins, Toc33 and Toc159 (Hirsch et al., 1994; Kessler et al., 1994; Perry and Keegstra, 1994; Jarvis et al., 1998; Jarvis, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Toc75 serves as a membrane channel.
source: the Omp85 (outer membrane protein, 85 kDa)-related protein, Toc75, which serves as a membrane channel (Schnell et al., 1994; Tranel et al., 1995)

claim: Toc33 and Toc159 project into the cytosol and bind incoming preproteins.

claim: The key components of the TOC complex were identified more than two decades ago.

evidence: This is a historical statement supported by citations to the original discovery papers.

claim: sp1 mutations partially suppress the phenotypic defects of ppi1 with respect to chlorosis, chloroplast development, and chloroplast protein import.

claim: SP2 and Cdc48 physically associate with SP1 and promote the membrane extraction of TOC proteins.

These are SP2, an Omp85-type β-barrel channel protein that was identified in the same genetic screen as SP1, and Cdc48, a well-characterized cytosolic AAA+ chaperone ATPase that provides the motive force for the extraction of proteins from the chloroplast outer envelope.

evidence: This is supported by chlorophyll measurements shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The ppi1 sum3-1 double mutant did not appear obviously different from the ppi1 control.
source: The resulting double mutant was phenotypically characterized, but it did not appear obviously different from the ppi1 control (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by visual observation shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The ppi1 sum3-1 double mutant did not display any clear increase in leaf chlorophyll concentration relative to ppi1.
source: Correspondingly, it did not display any clear increase in leaf chlorophyll concentration relative to ppi1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by chlorophyll measurements shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The ppi1 SUMO3 overexpression line showed a striking increase in the severity of the ppi1 phenotype: the plants were severely dwarfed and paler than the ppi1 control.
source: Interestingly, the transgenic plants showed a striking increase in the severity of the ppi1 phenotype: the plants were severely dwarfed and paler than the ppi1 control (Figure 4G)
evidence: This is supported by visual observation shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The ppi1 SUMO3 overexpression line displayed a significant decrease in leaf chlorophyll accumulation.
source: and displayed a significant decrease in leaf chlorophyll accumulation (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is supported by chlorophyll measurements shown in Figure 4H.

claim: SUMO3 overexpression was not found to alter the appearance of transgenic plants in wild-type background.
source: These findings are particularly noteworthy when considered alongside a previous report, which explored the consequences of overexpressing SUMO3 in wild-type plants (van den Burg et al., 2010). In that study, SUMO3 overexpression was not found to alter the appearance of the transgenic plants
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Protein SUMOylation was detected in isolated chloroplast samples.
source: Importantly, we detected protein SUMOylation in the isolated chloroplast samples, and this SUMOylation was increased by NEM treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Protein SUMOylation in isolated chloroplasts was increased by NEM treatment.
source: Importantly, we detected protein SUMOylation in the isolated chloroplast samples, and this SUMOylation was increased by NEM treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The SCE1-YFP fusion protein was found to be associated with native Toc159 and Toc132.
source: Remarkably, the SCE1-YFP fusion protein was found to be associated with native Toc159 and Toc132, but not with the negative control proteins Tic110 or Tic40 (Figure 5A; Kovacheva et al., 2005; Inaba et al., 2005 ).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The SCE1-YFP fusion protein was not associated with the negative control proteins Tic110 or Tic40.
source: Remarkably, the SCE1-YFP fusion protein was found to be associated with native Toc159 and Toc132, but not with the negative control proteins Tic110 or Tic40 (Figure 5A; Kovacheva et al., 2005; Inaba et al., 2005 ).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: YFP-HA did not associate with any of the tested proteins (Toc159, Toc132, Tic110, Tic40).
source: Conversely, YFP-HA did not associate with any of the tested proteins.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: All three YFP-SUMO proteins were found to physically associate with native Toc159.
source: Remarkably, all three YFP-SUMO proteins were found to physically associate with Toc159, although YFP-SUMO3 clearly bound Toc159 with the greatest affinity (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: YFP-SUMO3 bound Toc159 with the greatest affinity among the three SUMO isoforms.
source: Remarkably, all three YFP-SUMO proteins were found to physically associate with Toc159, although YFP-SUMO3 clearly bound Toc159 with the greatest affinity (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The YFP-HA negative control did not associate with Toc159.
source: In contrast with the SUMO fusions, the YFP-HA negative control did not associate with Toc159
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: None of the four YFP fusion proteins physically associated with Tic40.
source: and none of the four YFP fusion proteins physically associated with Tic40, a negative control protein (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: YFP-SUMO3 physically associated with Toc33-HA.
source: In accordance with the Toc159 result (Figure 5B), YFP-SUMO3, but not YFP-HA, was found to physically associate with Toc33-HA (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: YFP-HA did not physically associate with Toc33-HA.
source: In accordance with the Toc159 result (Figure 5B), YFP-SUMO3, but not YFP-HA, was found to physically associate with Toc33-HA (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Bands corresponding to the molecular weight of Toc33-HA bearing one, two, or several YFP-SUMO3 motifs were detected.
source: Moreover, bands of the exact expected molecular weight for Toc33-HA bearing one or two YFP-SUMO3 moieties (75 and 114 kDa) were also detected. These bands were accompanied by a high molecular weight smear at the top of the immunoblot, which is indicative of complex, multisite or chain SUMOylation.
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: A high molecular weight smear at the top of the immunoblot is indicative of complex, multisite or chain SUMOylation.
source: These bands were accompanied by a high molecular weight smear at the top of the immunoblot, which is indicative of complex, multisite or chain SUMOylation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunoblotting data based on established knowledge.

claim: SUMOylation acts to destabilize the TOC complex.
source: Thus, our results suggest that SUMOylation acts to destabilize the TOC complex, and that when such SUMOylation is perturbed the TOC proteins are stabilized.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: When SUMOylation is perturbed, TOC proteins are stabilized.
source: Thus, our results suggest that SUMOylation acts to destabilize the TOC complex, and that when such SUMOylation is perturbed the TOC proteins are stabilized.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: TOC complexes containing Toc34, Toc75, and Toc159 accumulate at higher levels in ppi1 / SUMO system double mutants.
source: We interpret that TOC complexes containing Toc34, Toc75, and Toc159 accumulate at higher levels in ppi1 / SUMO system double mutants, and that this synthetically improves the double mutant phenotypes relative to the ppi1 control.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Each core TOC protein was predicted with high probability to have one or more SUMOylation sites.
source: Importantly, each core TOC protein, including all of those analyzed in this study, was predicted with high probability to have one or more SUMOylation sites (Table 1; Zhao et al., 2014; Beauclair et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by bioinformatic analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: The ppi1 suppression effects mediated by SUMO system mutations are remarkably similar to those mediated by the sp1 and sp2 mutations.
source: The ppi1 suppression effects described here are remarkably similar to those mediated by the sp1 and sp2 mutations (Ling et al., 2012; Ling et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work supported by citations.

claim: Like sp1 and sp2, SUMO system mutations can partially suppress ppi1 with respect to chlorophyll concentration, TOC protein accumulation, and chloroplast development.
source: Like sp1 and sp2, SUMO system mutations can partially suppress ppi1 with respect to chlorophyll concentration, TOC protein accumulation, and chloroplast development.
evidence: This is a comparison to previous work.

claim: SUMOylation may regulate the activity of the CHLORAD pathway.
source: This similarity suggests that SUMOylation may regulate the activity of the CHLORAD pathway.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the similarity of phenotypes.

claim: Both SUMOylation and the CHLORAD pathway are activated by various forms of environmental stress.
source: This is an attractive hypothesis as both SUMOylation and the CHLORAD pathway are activated by various forms of environmental stress (Kurepa et al., 2003; Ling and Jarvis, 2015; Ling et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The SUMOylation of TOC proteins may promote their CHLORAD-mediated degradation.
source: One possibility is that the SUMOylation of TOC proteins promotes their CHLORAD-mediated degradation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The ability to carry out SUMOylation is negatively correlated with the stability of TOC proteins in the context of the developed plants studied here.
source: Indeed, as already noted, the ability to carry out SUMOylation is negatively correlated with the stability of TOC proteins in the context of the developed plants studied here.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: SUMOylation can both promote and antagonize the effects of ubiquitination in different situations.
source: However, it should be kept in mind that SUMOylation can both promote and antagonize the effects of ubiquitination in different situations (Desterro et al., 1998; Ahner et al., 2013; Liebelt and Vertegaal, 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Toc159 receptor is regulated by SP1 when integrated into the outer envelope membrane.
source: The Toc159 receptor is regulated by SP1 when integrated into the outer envelope membrane (Ling et al., 2012; Ling et al., 2019)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Toc159 receptor is regulated by a different E3 ligase when it exists as a cytosolic precursor during the earliest stages of development before germination.
source: but by a different E3 ligase when it exists as a cytosolic precursor during the earliest stages of development before germination (Shanmugabalaji et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The precise mechanisms underpinning the observed negative regulation of the TOC apparatus by SUMOylation are currently unknown.
source: The precise mechanisms underpinning the observed negative regulation of the TOC apparatus by SUMOylation are currently unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: SUMOylation can modify protein-protein interactions.
source: SUMOylation can modify protein-protein interactions
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: Some RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligases specifically recognize SUMOylated substrates.
source: and some RING-type E3 ubiquitin ligases specifically recognize SUMOylated substrates (Sriramachandran and Dohmen, 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: SUMO-targeted ubiquitin ligases (STUbLs) typically contain SUMO-interacting motifs (SIMs).
source: However, these SUMO-targeted ubiquitin ligases (STUbLs) typically contain SUMO-interacting motifs (SIMs), which guide the ligases to SUMO proteins conjugated to their substrates
evidence: This is established knowledge.

claim: SIMs are not apparent in SP1.
source: and these are not apparent in SP1 (data not shown; Zhao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis by the authors.

claim: SP1 forms a complex with SP2 and very likely additional cofactors.
source: However, SP1 forms a complex with SP2 and very likely additional cofactors
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work.

claim: Ufd1 contains a SIM, which can guide Cdc48 to SUMOylated proteins.
source: Two important Cdc48 cofactors are Ufd1 and Npl4, and the former contains a SIM, which can guide Cdc48 to SUMOylated proteins (Nie et al., 2012; Baek et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The SUMO-mediated recruitment of Cdc48 has important roles in the maintenance of genome stability in yeast.
source: Moreover, the SUMO-mediated recruitment of Cdc48 has important roles in the maintenance of genome stability in yeast (Bergink et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Of the three SUMO isoforms tested, SUMO3 binds TOC proteins with the highest affinity.
source: The biochemical experiments described in this article indicate that, of the three SUMO isoforms tested, SUMO3 binds TOC proteins with the highest affinity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the IP experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There is an apparent incongruence between the results of the biochemical experiments and the results of the genetic experiments regarding SUMO3.
source: However, there is an apparent incongruence between the results of these experiments and the results of the genetic experiments.
evidence: This is an observation about the data.

claim: The sum1-1 and sum2-1 mutants were found to additively suppress ppi1.
source: While the sum1-1 and sum2-1 mutants were found to additively suppress ppi1, the sum3-1 mutant did not suppress ppi1.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The sum3-1 mutant did not suppress ppi1.
source: While the sum1-1 and sum2-1 mutants were found to additively suppress ppi1, the sum3-1 mutant did not suppress ppi1.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E-F.

claim: SUMO1 and SUMO2 are highly abundant relative to SUMO3, which is, at steady state, very weakly abundant.
source: SUMO1 and SUMO2 are highly abundant relative to SUMO3, which is, at steady state, very weakly abundant (van den Burg et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: SUMO1 and SUMO2 can weakly interact with Toc159.
source: The IP data shown in Figure 5B indicated that SUMO1 and SUMO2 can weakly interact with Toc159
evidence: This is supported by IP data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: SUMO1 and SUMO2 can compensate for the loss of SUMO3 in the sum3-1 mutant.
source: and so it is likely that these two isoforms can compensate for the loss of SUMO3 in the sum3-1 mutant.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the genetic data.

claim: When overexpressed, SUMO3 accentuates the ppi1 phenotype to a far greater extent than does SUMO1.
source: It is also noteworthy that, when overexpressed, SUMO3 accentuates the ppi1 phenotype to a far greater extent than does SUMO1.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C-D and 4G-H.

claim: The regulation of chloroplast protein import has critical roles in plant development and stress acclimation.
source: It is now well established that the regulation of chloroplast protein import has critical roles in plant development and stress acclimation (Sowden et al., 2018; Watson et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The results are consistent with a model in which SUMOylation modulates the activity or effects of the CHLORAD pathway.
source: Here, we demonstrate regulatory crosstalk between the SUMO system and the chloroplast protein import machinery, and present results that are consistent with a model in which SUMOylation modulates the activity or effects of the CHLORAD pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.
